title: Bleed Isolation Valve Actuator — Removal

issue.reason: Original issue of the bleed isolation valve actuator removal task.

abstract: Removal of the bleed isolation valve actuator and its position regulator from the pylon, including the duct cool-down time and the rigging record that must be taken before the actuator is disturbed.

sections.purpose: To remove the isolation valve actuator and its matched position regulator from the engine, cross-bleed or ground connection position for replacement.
sections.job_setup_note: The engine must have been shut down for at least ninety minutes so that the duct is cool. The fan cowl must be open and supported. Two persons are needed. The rigging position must be recorded before anything is loosened, because the replacement actuator is set to the recorded value rather than to a nominal one.
sections.procedure: WARNING: DO NOT TOUCH THE BLEED DUCT UNTIL AT LEAST NINETY MINUTES AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THE DUCT SURFACE CAN CAUSE SEVERE BURNS. Put the safety barriers in position and open the fan cowl. Support the cowl on the hold-open rod. Remove the electrical power from the aircraft and put the warning notices in position. Record the actuator rigging position against the scale on the valve body and write the value on the removal tag. Disconnect the electrical connector at the actuator and fit the protective cap. Disconnect the position regulator harness. CAUTION: DO NOT LEVER THE ACTUATOR OFF THE VALVE BODY. THE DRIVE SPLINE IS EASILY DAMAGED AND THE VALVE BODY WILL HAVE TO BE REPLACED. Loosen the four actuator flange bolts in a diagonal sequence and remove them. Pull the actuator squarely off the drive spline. Remove the position regulator from its bracket and disconnect the sensing line. Cap the sensing line and the valve port immediately. Remove the swaged collars from the duct joint if the joint is to be broken. Put the removed units in the transit container with the rigging tag attached.
sections.close_out: Make sure that all ports and connectors are capped. Make sure that no tools or loose hardware remain in the pylon. Fit the blanking cover to the valve drive if the actuator is not being replaced immediately. Close the fan cowl if no further work is planned. Record the removal, the serial numbers and the recorded rigging value.

safety_precautions: Do not touch the bleed duct until at least ninety minutes after engine shutdown.
Put the safety barriers in position.
Support the fan cowl on the hold-open rod.

title: Bleed Isolation Valve Actuator — Removal

issue.reason: Disconnection and capping of the valve position sensor connector added, which did not exist when the task was written.

abstract: Removal of the bleed isolation valve actuator and its position regulator from the pylon, including the duct cool-down time, the position sensor disconnection and the rigging record that must be taken before the actuator is disturbed.

sections.purpose: To remove the isolation valve actuator and its matched position regulator from the engine, cross-bleed or ground connection position for replacement.
sections.job_setup_note: The engine must have been shut down for at least ninety minutes so that the duct is cool. The fan cowl must be open and supported. Two persons are needed. The rigging position must be recorded before anything is loosened, because the replacement actuator is set to the recorded value rather than to a nominal one. Establish whether the aircraft is at the four-position standard: on those aircraft a position sensor sits on the valve body beside the actuator and has to be disconnected first.
sections.procedure: WARNING: DO NOT TOUCH THE BLEED DUCT UNTIL AT LEAST NINETY MINUTES AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THE DUCT SURFACE CAN CAUSE SEVERE BURNS. Put the safety barriers in position and open the fan cowl. Support the cowl on the hold-open rod. Remove the electrical power from the aircraft and put the warning notices in position. Record the actuator rigging position against the scale on the valve body and write the value on the removal tag. Disconnect the electrical connector at the actuator and fit the protective cap. Disconnect the position regulator harness. On an aircraft at the four-position standard, disconnect the valve position sensor GIR634074-45 at the boss connector and fit the cap to both halves; the sensor stays on the valve body and is not removed with the actuator, and its lead is long enough to be pulled taut and damaged if the actuator is drawn off while it is still connected. CAUTION: DO NOT LEVER THE ACTUATOR OFF THE VALVE BODY. THE DRIVE SPLINE IS EASILY DAMAGED AND THE VALVE BODY WILL HAVE TO BE REPLACED. Loosen the four actuator flange bolts in a diagonal sequence and remove them. Pull the actuator squarely off the drive spline. Remove the position regulator from its bracket and disconnect the sensing line. Cap the sensing line and the valve port immediately. Remove the swaged collars from the duct joint if the joint is to be broken. Put the removed units in the transit container with the rigging tag attached.
sections.close_out: Make sure that all ports and connectors are capped, including the position sensor boss connector where one is fitted. Make sure that no tools or loose hardware remain in the pylon. Fit the blanking cover to the valve drive if the actuator is not being replaced immediately. Close the fan cowl if no further work is planned. Record the removal, the serial numbers and the recorded rigging value.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The position sensor disconnection applies only to aircraft at the four-position standard.

safety_precautions: Do not touch the bleed duct until at least ninety minutes after engine shutdown.
Put the safety barriers in position.
Support the fan cowl on the hold-open rod.
